## Welcome to EMSC-2010

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Learn to Ask Better Questions — and Find Meaningful Answers

Data science is the most powerful tool we have for separating scientific fact from fiction. This course will teach you to interpret data, assess uncertainty, model outcomes, and make informed decisions about real Earth and Environmental science problems.
:::

### Quick Links

- [**About this Course**](about.qmd) - Full course information, learning outcomes, and structure
- [**Construction Plan**](construction-plan.qmd) - Current development status and roadmap
- [**Course Materials**](intro.qmd) - Lecture notes, practicals, and resources (under development)

## What You'll Learn

This course is built around five key questions:

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Prediction
**"How can I make predictions of the future?"**

Learn time series analysis, trend detection, and forecasting methods using real climate and environmental data.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Optimization
**"Where should I expend effort to improve results?"**

Master sensitivity analysis, error propagation, and resource allocation strategies for field studies and monitoring.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Measurement
**"What accuracy and how many measurements do I need?"**

Apply sample size determination, power analysis, and measurement error assessment to real sampling problems.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Significance
**"Is this result meaningful, or just random chance?"**

Understand hypothesis testing, statistical significance, and how to separate signal from noise in Earth science data.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Causation
**"Why is this happening and what's driving the change?"**

Explore correlation vs. causation, attribution methods, and multivariate analysis for understanding Earth system processes.
:::

:::

## Course Structure

### Three-Phase Learning Design

::: {.callout-tip}
## Phase 1: Build Your Foundation (Weeks 1-4)
**Mastery learning** with unlimited quiz attempts ensures all students develop essential data science skills: critical thinking, algorithmic problem-solving, statistical analysis, hypothesis testing, and working with data.

- 2 × 2-hour practicals per week
- 1 × 1-hour tutorial per week
- Weekly quizzes (hurdle requirement)
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Phase 2: Apply Collaboratively (Weeks 5-12)
Work in teams on **problems you choose** from Earth and Environmental Sciences. Learn modern collaborative workflows.

- 2-hour lectorial per week
- 3-hour practical per week
- GitHub collaborative project
- Team lab notebooks
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Phase 3: Demonstrate Independence (Weeks 8-12 + Exam Period)
Tackle an individual project from planning through to presentation, building on your team experience.

- Individual project plan
- Project execution
- Final report (due Week 12)
- Project showcase (exam period)
:::

---

## Key Features

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Student Choice
Select problems that are **relevant and exciting to you** - climate change, earthquakes, water resources, mineral exploration, or any Earth science question you care about.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Modern Tools
Learn Python, Git/GitHub, Jupyter notebooks, and data visualization - the same tools used in real research and industry.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Equity-Focused
**All students, not just the best**, master essential skills through unlimited attempts and comprehensive support.
:::

:::
